subject: New telemetry vendor proposed — subprocessor questionnaire & required evidence
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <legalops@payport.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Anders <security@payport.io>
Date: 2024-05-22T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed telemetry collector subprocessor — short notice

Hi Irene,

Hope you’re doing well. PayPort is appointing a new telemetry aggregator (Collectra Inc.) to capture anonymized runtime metrics from our sandboxed integrations. We wanted to give Redwood a heads-up and provide the vendor roster extract for your review (attached).

Quick details:
- Purpose: aggregated telemetry (latency metrics, anonymized error rates, SDK version counts)
- Data types: no PII, only hashed identifiers and telemetry payloads
- Location: Collectra maintains EU and US endpoints; primary processing in us-east1
- Expected start date: 2024-06-01 (pilot)

Request: please confirm any evidence or attestations Redwood requires for this subprocessor (SOC2 type II, encryption-in-transit details, cross-border controls). We’ve copied Security (Tom) on this thread.

Attachments: telemetry_vendor_roster.csv

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Legal Ops — PayPort
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <legalops@payport.io>
Cc: Tom Anders <security@payport.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-05-22T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed telemetry collector subprocessor — short notice

Elena — thanks for the heads-up and the roster. A couple of quick asks so we can triage internally: 

1) Please confirm that Collectra will not receive any raw customer content (only runtime telemetry).
2) Provide their SOC 2 report or a recent security attestation (last 12 months).
3) Clarify where hashed identifiers are derived (client-side or server-side) and whether salts/pepper are used.
4) If processing will hit EU systems, we’ll need details on transfer mechanisms (SCCs / other).

I’ll loop in Product for impact on integrations and Security for technical evidence. If PayPort wants a faster path, a short vendor questionnaire + the SOC2 PDF usually suffices.

Best,
Irene Choi
Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <legalops@payport.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-05-22T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed telemetry collector subprocessor — short notice

Thanks Irene / Elena — product note: if Collectra is only ingesting telemetry we can gate it behind a config flag per-customer (so PayPort can enable it for a pilot account) while we complete the evidence review.

Operational asks from our side:
- A short data-flow diagram showing exactly what fields flow to Collectra (one page).
- Expected QPS and retention period for the telemetry payloads.

Elena, if you can share the one-pager + the SOC2 doc we’ll fast-track a limited pilot approval.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Integrations
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <legalops@payport.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-05-23T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed telemetry collector subprocessor — short notice

Elena — pulled the roster and did a quick scan. A few technical clarifications we need before any pilot: 

- TLS version and cipher suites for ingestion endpoints. We require TLS1.2+ and AEAD ciphers.
- Whether JWTs / API keys used are scoped per-customer and whether they support key rotation.
- Data-at-rest encryption details for the US processing region (KMS provider, key rotation cadence).
- Proof that Collectra does not attempt to re-identify hashed identifiers (policy statement or clause).

I’ve attached a template attestation we typically request — if Collectra can sign/return that plus their SOC2 PDF we can clear them for a limited pilot behind an account-level toggle.

Attachments: vendor-security-attestation.pdf

Regards,
Ben Carter
Security Engineering (Integrations)
Redwood Inference
From: Tom Anders <security@payport.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <legalops@payport.io>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2024-05-23T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed telemetry collector subprocessor — short notice

Ben / team — attaching the SOC2 and the initial data flow diagram to this reply (see Drive link below). Collectra confirms:
- No raw customer content will be forwarded; hashed identifiers are generated client-side with a per-customer salt.
- TLS 1.2+ with recommended AEAD suites; data-at-rest encrypted with AWS KMS (customer-managed keys supported).
- Collectra signed the attestation and is open to a narrow pilot.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-payport-evidence
DocuSign (attestation): https://www.docusign.com/collectra-attest

Elena Ruiz
Legal Ops — PayPort
